A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SCILLA study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete supplementary material support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original reconstruction results on four driving datasets, component ablations, and supplementary qualitative experiments on Tanks and Temples.

after.justification: V3 retains original reconstruction experiments and reports additional baseline comparisons, convergence experiments, and sensitivity analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 reverses the specified sample-attribution rule: v1 assigns SDF-based alpha values first to the lowest-density samples, whereas v3 assigns them to the highest-density samples. This changes a specific initialization component; the hybrid architecture, three training stages, rendering equations, and losses remain otherwise unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same four driving datasets and retain the Auditorium, Temple, Truck, and Meetingroom examples from Tanks and Temples. Additional experiments use existing driving-scene coverage; Neuralangelo segmentation and image-count variations concern evaluation procedures.

E2.justification: V1 primarily compares reconstruction against StreetSurf. V3 adds COLMAP and OpenMVS to quantitative, qualitative, and efficiency comparisons, and reports original qualitative Neuralangelo trials in supplementary Section 8. OpenMVS's earlier use for texturing meshes was not a reconstruction-baseline evaluation.

E3.justification: V3 introduces density-versus-SDF convergence comparisons using Chamfer distance without normal supervision, hybrid-duration experiments at 10%, 35%, 50%, and 65%, and Neuralangelo trials varying spherical bounds, scene segmentation, and image counts. Table 2 replaces iteration time with total training time. The main 14k-iteration budget and reconstruction metric definitions remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The single-scene component ablation in v1 Table 3 becomes a four-scene numerical comparison spanning all driving datasets. V3 Figure 6 adds direct density-versus-SDF convergence evidence and hybrid-duration sensitivity, while supplementary Section 8 investigates Neuralangelo failures under alternative configurations. The random-versus-probability attribution experiment and SCILLA failure cases already existed in v1.

E5.justification: V1 Figure 5 visibly includes standard-deviation bands for KITTI-360 and nuScenes; v3 Figure 4 additionally displays them for Pandaset and Waymo. These describe variation across scenes, not repeated training runs. Neither version reports seed-based uncertainty or significance testing.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises many retained scores: KITTI-360 sequence 30 P-to-mesh error changes from 0.13 to 0.18 m for SCILLA and from 0.14 to 0.19 m for StreetSurf. V3 adds MVS results, expanded ablation scores, convergence curves, and Neuralangelo failure outcomes. Table 2 reports total times of 20 and 40 minutes for SCILLA and StreetSurf. The supplementary Neuralangelo training-time comparison changes from 10 to 24 hours. These revisions do not establish a same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: The rendering, SDF, normal-supervision, and regularization mathematics are retained. V1's gradient-normalization derivation and Equation 5 move to supplementary Section 7 and Equation 9 in v3. Additional conceptual explanations do not introduce new formal results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims of hybrid image-based surface reconstruction, initialization without strong scene-geometric priors, detailed driving-scene reconstruction, and approximately twofold training efficiency. V3's emphasis on progressive initialization restates an existing contribution.

C2.justification: V3 replaces the low-density, coarse-to-fine attribution rationale with an explanation based on restricting SDF predictions near surfaces. It also interprets hybrid-duration sensitivity, MVS precision and completeness tradeoffs, and Neuralangelo's dependence on bounded scenes and overlapping images. SCILLA's three supplementary limitations remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: Supplementary Section 9 newly documents Waymo trajectory and calibration recomputation with MOISST, frame subsampling rates, and KITTI synchronization identifiers in Table 5. V3 also identifies the MVS reconstruction pipelines and Neuralangelo code source. These improve reproducibility documentation without establishing that the retained experiments' preprocessing changed between versions.

R1.justification: V3 adds references to MOISST and Jancosek and Pajdla's visibility-based reconstruction, and expands positioning against Neuralangelo's bounded landmark setting. Most related work remains intact. The Pixelwise View Selection paper cited for COLMAP was already referenced in v1.

P1.justification: V3 makes local prose revisions, emphasizes progressive initialization terminology, introduces explicit experimental subsections, and moves the gradient-normalization explanation into the supplement. References move after the supplementary material, but the main narrative and much of the wording remain recognizable.

P2.justification: V3 adopts a two-column layout, consolidates qualitative comparisons into grids with additional baseline columns, and expands and color-codes tables. It removes v1's sample-attribution schematic and Table 3's spatial error maps, while adding convergence plots and Neuralangelo illustrations. Some labels regress: v3 Figure 5 labels retained Waymo examples as sequences 71 and 916 rather than 10061 and 102751.

improvement.justification: V1's broad reconstruction and convergence arguments relied mainly on StreetSurf comparisons and a single-scene component ablation. V3 substantially strengthens their empirical support through MVS comparisons, documented Neuralangelo trials, direct convergence controls, and ablations across four datasets. Added preprocessing details and uncertainty bands improve assessability. Incorrect Waymo figure labels and percentage notation in the new precision summary are drawbacks, but their impact is limited relative to the stronger validation.
